record.title: EDGEGEN reports gains from specification-derived edge-case tasks for tool-calling agents
record.summary: EDGEGEN extracts compliance rules from an agent specification, combines structured rule-violation scenarios with executable database states, and uses the generated tasks for fine-tuning or harness optimization. The authors report improvement over the base model in all 18 model–benchmark comparisons across three benchmarks; on tau2-bench Airline they report relative mean-progress gains ranging from 2% to 42%, while one harness-optimization result for Gemma-4-e4b is 10% above human-curated and 30% above the base harness. Main evaluations use only 10–15 scenarios per benchmark. In a small audit, human reviewers confirmed only 6 of 10 Airline and 4 of 10 ToolSandbox runs labeled successful. These are preprint-reported results, not independently reproduced evidence of general agent reliability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that fine-tuning on EDGEGEN-generated tasks improves mean progress over the base model in all 18 model–benchmark pairs spanning tau2-bench Airline, Retail and ToolSandbox; reported relative gains on Airline range from about 2% to 42%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For Gemma-4-e4b on tau2-bench Airline, the authors report harness optimization with EDGEGEN tasks yields mean progress 10% above the human-curated optimized harness and 30% above the base harness.

evidence_gaps.description: Main evaluations use 10–15 scenarios per benchmark. In a small human audit of runs labeled successful, reviewers judged only 6/10 Airline and 4/10 ToolSandbox runs correct; assertion omissions and judge errors were among the failures.

The evidence is an author-run preprint study across three benchmark domains; results are not independently reproduced, gains are not uniform for every harness result, and applicability to coding or web-navigation agents is untested.

brief.importance_rationale: If the approach generalizes, policy-derived and database-grounded tasks could improve how tool agents are tested and fine-tuned for rule-sensitive workflows. A 5 reflects practical relevance to agent evaluation and training; results remain a single preprint's small-sample experiments and imperfect task/judge validation.
limitations: The preprint reports small main evaluation sets of 10–15 scenarios per benchmark; supplementary scaling uses 21 Airline scenarios.
Human reviewers confirmed only 6/10 sampled Airline and 4/10 ToolSandbox runs that the system marked successful; task assertions and automated judging can be wrong.
Rule extraction and database grounding do not guarantee that generated tasks encode the policy correctly; the appendix gives a policy-rule misalignment example.
Reported gains do not establish uniform improvement: harness optimization on ToolSandbox was below the human-curated result, and one Gemma harness result slightly degraded.
Applicability to coding and web-navigation agents is untested; no independent reproduction was conducted.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report improved mean progress over base in all 18 model–benchmark pairs; Airline fine-tuning gains range from about 2% to 42%. A Gemma-4-e4b Airline harness result is reported 10% above the human-curated optimized harness and 30% above base.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint documents the method, comparisons and audit; performance values are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
technical.mechanism: Extract up to five prioritized compliance rules from an agent policy, enumerate feasible combinations of rule violations, ground user requests and workflows in executable database states, filter infeasible cases, and use generated successful trajectories for fine-tuning or harness optimization.
technical.regime: Three benchmark domains (tau2-bench Airline and Retail, ToolSandbox), multiple model families. Main evaluations use 10–15 scenarios per benchmark; human correctness review sampled 10 successful-labeled runs each for Airline and ToolSandbox.
technical.reproducibility: Full arXiv v1 HTML and appendices inspected. No independent reproduction; larger held-out suites and task/judge audits remain needed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Base model/harness, generic synthetic task generation, human-curated training examples, TaskBench and FuncBenchGen comparisons as reported in the paper.

brief.title: EDGEGEN reports gains from specification-derived edge-case tasks for tool-calling agents
brief.why_it_matters: Policy-conditioned, database-grounded tasks could expose tool-agent failures that generic happy-path prompts miss and could provide training examples for policy compliance. The reported gains are bounded by small evaluation samples, imperfect automated judgments, selected benchmarks and author-run experiments.
